plates.title: Map of the Replication Crisis
plates.prompt: An antique hand-inked map in sepia and faded blue-green wash, aged parchment paper with soft foxing at the edges, in the style of a 16th-century atlas page annotated with small pictorial vignettes rather than text blocks. Top of the page: a toppling stack of papers scattering pages (TOPPLING STACK), beside a lexicon stand with a scholar and magnifying glass (GLOSSARY STONE). Below, a calendar scroll unrolling into three pinned scenes of an elderly walker, a card-table, and a lab mouse (EVENTS OF THE EARLY 2010s), leading to robed scholars raising a cracked seal before a broken column (CRISIS OF CONFIDENCE), and behind them three old sages writing unheeded warnings while a storm gathers (THE UNHEEDED SAGES). The map then opens into a wide convergence zone labeled only by imagery: a field of 97 small flags mostly fallen (97 FLAGS, FEW STANDING), a shelf of 53 jars mostly cracked open (53 JARS, FEW SEALED), and two ledgers with shrinking coin-stacks (SHRUNKEN LEDGERS) — all three paths flowing down into a great crossroads gathering of robed researchers shaking their heads over empty flasks (THE GATHERING OF FAILURES). From that crossroads the map forks into two descending valleys: on the left, a locked drawer stuffed with discarded papers (THE FILE DRAWER) and a figure choosing among many garden gates (THE GARDEN OF CHOICES); on the right, a torn recipe scroll missing half its words (THE TORN RECIPE) and a tilting balance-scale sinking into soft ground (SCALES ON SOFT GROUND). The two valleys converge again at the bottom into two final opposing figures shouting across a table, one accusing, one inspecting with a magnifying glass (THE QUARREL AT THE TABLE), then a scholar nailing an open unsealed scroll to a post in daylight (THE OPEN SCROLL), and finally three instruments — a compass, a scale, a sundial — all pointing to the same spot (THREE INSTRUMENTS AGREE). Compass roses, faint coastlines, and fine cross-hatching fill empty paper sparingly; no lettering anywhere except the sixteen titles lettered in small antique capitals directly beneath each vignette.

vignettes.quote: widespread failures to reproduce published scientific results
vignettes.depicts: A toppling stack of published papers, pages scattering as the stack collapses, at the top of the map like a broken monument.
vignettes.title: THE TOPPLING STACK

vignettes.quote: Certain terms commonly used in discussions of the replication crisis have technically precise meanings
vignettes.depicts: A small lexicon stand bearing carved words like P-VALUE and POWER, a scholar consulting it with a magnifying glass.
vignettes.title: GLOSSARY STONE

vignettes.quote: The replication crisis dates to a number of events in the early 2010s
vignettes.depicts: A calendar scroll unrolling to show the early 2010s, with three small scenes pinned to it — an elderly walker, a card-guessing table, a mouse in a lab.
vignettes.title: EVENTS OF THE EARLY 2010S

vignettes.quote: led prominent scholars to declare a "crisis of confidence" in psychology and other fields
vignettes.depicts: Robed scholars raising a banner reading nothing but drawn as a cracked seal, standing before a cracked column labeled with no text, declaring alarm.
vignettes.title: CRISIS OF CONFIDENCE

vignettes.quote: the works of Paul Meehl, Jacob Cohen, and Tversky and Kahneman in the 1960s-70s were early warnings
vignettes.depicts: Three old sages at desks decades earlier, writing unheeded warnings into ledgers while a storm gathers unseen behind them.
vignettes.title: THE UNHEEDED SAGES

vignettes.quote: Of 97 original studies with significant effects, 36% replicated successfully
vignettes.depicts: A field of 97 small flags, only about a third standing upright and the rest fallen flat in the grass.
vignettes.title: 97 FLAGS, FEW STANDING

vignettes.quote: only 11% of 53 pre-clinical cancer studies had replications that could confirm conclusions
vignettes.depicts: A row of 53 sealed jars on a laboratory shelf, nearly all cracked open and empty, a handful still sealed.
vignettes.title: 53 JARS, FEW SEALED

vignettes.quote: approximately 61% of studies successfully replicated, though the replicated effect sizes were only 66% of the original reported effect sizes
vignettes.depicts: Two ledgers side by side, coins stacked taller in the original column than in the replication column beside it.
vignettes.title: SHRUNKEN LEDGERS

vignettes.quote: more than 70% of researchers have tried and failed to reproduce another scientist's experiment results
vignettes.depicts: A great gathering of robed researchers at a crossroads where all the field-paths meet, most shaking their heads over empty flasks.
vignettes.title: THE GATHERING OF FAILURES

vignettes.quote: Publication bias—the tendency to publish only positive, significant results—creates the "file drawer effect"
vignettes.depicts: A locked cabinet drawer stuffed with discarded papers, while only the bright ones on top are laid out on a desk for display.
vignettes.title: THE FILE DRAWER

vignettes.quote: articles often come with insufficient descriptions for other scholars to reproduce the study
vignettes.depicts: A thin, torn recipe scroll with half its instructions missing, held up by a puzzled reader trying to follow it.
vignettes.title: THE TORN RECIPE

vignettes.quote: null hypothesis testing is itself inappropriate, especially in "soft sciences" like social psychology
vignettes.depicts: A balance-scale tilting oddly on soft, sinking ground, unable to weigh anything properly.
vignettes.title: SCALES ON SOFT GROUND

vignettes.quote: called these unidentified "adversaries" names such as "methodological terrorist" and "self-appointed data police"
vignettes.depicts: Two opposing figures shouting across a table, one pointing an accusing finger, the other holding a magnifying glass over a paper.
vignettes.title: THE QUARREL AT THE TABLE

vignettes.quote: may include emphasizing transparency and openness, preregistering research projects
vignettes.depicts: A scholar nailing an open, unsealed scroll to a public post before any experiment begins, in full daylight.
vignettes.title: THE OPEN SCROLL

plates.title: Many Seas, One Tide
plates.prompt: An antique hand-inked map in sepia and faded blue-green wash on aged parchment, continuing the same atlas style. At the top, eight separate coastal inlets, each a different field of study rendered as a small vignette: a field of mostly-fallen flags (97 FLAGS, FEW STANDING); a tiny spark surrounded by thousands of gathered lanterns (THOUSANDS OF LANTERNS); a bench of tipped-over vials with an idle robot arm (THE TIPPED VIALS); 49 physician's scrolls stamped 'effective' with contradicting scrolls shadowed behind (49 PHYSICIAN SCROLLS); an open cookbook with circled ingredients (THE CIRCLED COOKBOOK); two ledgers of coin-stacks, the second shorter (SHRUNKEN LEDGERS); a dried riverbed of cracked charts with one trickle (THE DRIED RIVERBED); and a strange oracle-machine giving different answers each time (THE SHIFTING ORACLE). All eight inlets' currents are drawn flowing downward and inward, joining at the center of the page into one great tide — a harbor crowded with robed figures from every shore, most carrying empty nets (THE CONVERGING TIDE). From that harbor, a single final current flows further down to a glowing broken scroll being copied far more eagerly than the sound scrolls beside it (THE BRIGHTER BROKEN SCROLL), drawn at the very bottom of the map as an ironic coda. Fine cross-hatched waves, faint compass roses, and small sailing ships mark the empty sea between inlets, but the page stays uncluttered, the vignettes large and legible. No lettering anywhere except the ten titles in small antique capitals beneath each vignette.

vignettes.depicts: A field of 97 small flags, roughly a third upright, the rest fallen.

vignettes.quote: approximately 61% of studies successfully replicated, though the replicated effect sizes were only 66% of the original reported effect sizes

vignettes.depicts: A dried-up riverbed of water-management charts, almost all cracked and unusable, a single trickle still flowing.

vignettes.quote: their outputs can shift from one run to the next even when settings are held constant
vignettes.depicts: A strange oracle-machine giving a different answer each time the same question is asked of it.
vignettes.title: THE SHIFTING ORACLE

vignettes.quote: papers that cannot be replicated are more likely to be cited
vignettes.depicts: A broken, unreplicated scroll glowing brighter and being copied more often than the sound scrolls beside it.
vignettes.title: THE BRIGHTER BROKEN SCROLL

plates.title: Two Shores of Causes
plates.prompt: An antique hand-inked map in sepia and faded blue-green wash, same atlas style as before, this plate showing two parallel coastal shores running down the page, divided by a thin inked channel. At the head of the channel, framing both shores, a small overflowing printing press spewing endless scrolls (THE OVERFLOWING PRESS), echoing the outer map's crossroads gathering. Down the left shore, labeled only by its own imagery: a locked drawer crammed with discarded papers beside a desk of bright ones (THE FILE DRAWER); a scribe's ledger with numbers that do not add up and a stray ink blot (THE MISCOUNTED LEDGER); a scholar racing a treadmill of stacked journals whipped on by a tally-keeper (THE PUBLISHING TREADMILL); a torn recipe scroll missing half its instructions (THE TORN RECIPE). Down the right shore: a traveler at a forking garden path trying gate after gate (THE GARDEN OF CHOICES); a weak lantern casting barely a third of needed light in a dark room (THE DIM LANTERN); a small object casting an oversized shadow on a wall (THE OVERSIZED SHADOW); a scholar stitching a patchwork quilt with mismatched seams (THE MISMATCHED QUILT); identical seeds sprouting into strangely different plants across different soils (SEEDS IN DIFFERENT SOIL); and at the very bottom of the right shore, a balance-scale tilting on soft sinking ground (SCALES ON SOFT GROUND). The two shores run side by side down the page without merging, each vignette large and clear, separated by the thin inked channel with small wave-hatching. Faint compass rose in a corner, light foxing at the page edges, no clutter in the margins. No lettering anywhere except the eleven titles in small antique capitals lettered directly beneath each vignette.

vignettes.quote: generation of new data and scientific publications at an unprecedented rate
vignettes.depicts: A overflowing printing press spewing out endless scrolls faster than any scribe can read them.
vignettes.title: THE OVERFLOWING PRESS

vignettes.depicts: A locked drawer crammed with discarded null-result papers beside a desk displaying only the bright successful ones.

vignettes.quote: psychology studies have between 33.1% and 36.4% statistical power

vignettes.quote: Intense pressure to publish in recognized journals, driven by hypercompetitive environments and bibliometric career evaluations

vignettes.quote: Meta-analyses have their own methodological problems and disputes
